before: **KEY:** Endoscopically assisted manometry
Junction-crossing manometry can provide the relaxation and body measurements absent from this recording. Assisted placement addresses the documented technical failure.
Timed barium esophagram with a barium tablet
Emptying and tablet passage can corroborate obstruction, but the prior contrast study already shows retention and this does not provide the missing manometric phenotype.
Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance monitoring
Regurgitation can tempt reflux testing, but it does not resolve junction relaxation and contractile classification after this technically failed pressure study.
after: **KEY:** Endoscopically assisted manometry
Junction-crossing manometry can provide the relaxation and body measurements absent from this recording. Assisted placement addresses the documented technical failure.

Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance monitoring

contextRevisions.inference: Recognize why simultaneous pressure in a recording confined above the diaphragm cannot establish the junction phenotype. Then Select technically assisted pressure acquisition rather than substitute an emptying or reflux study.
contextRevisions.focus: Motility review must confirm assisted placement feasibility after this retching-limited attempt. No universal HRM-before-FLIP hierarchy or sedation-acquisition rule is asserted.

before: **KEY:** Refer during ongoing rehabilitation
The remaining functional interruption tracks the reducible protrusion despite improvement in the coexisting attachment/joint symptoms. Elective assessment need not await completion of that treatment.
Refer after rehabilitation is completed
Residual musculoskeletal symptoms can coexist with a hernia that already limits function. Treating them first as an absolute referral prerequisite delays the separately supported hernia assessment.
Refer after repeat imaging documents progression
Anatomical enlargement is not required before discussing an already demonstrated activity-limiting inguinal hernia. This mistakes imaging change for the relevant functional criterion.
after: **KEY:** Hip-focused musculoskeletal assessment

The limiting low-shelf task and reproduced deep ache now track hip movement while the visible protrusion is tolerated. Prior hernia-related episodes do not establish the cause of this different remaining limitation.
Hernia-focused surgical assessment
The demonstrated hernia and earlier lifting episodes make this credible, but the later functional record does not connect the remaining low-shelf limitation to current protrusion episodes.
Pubic-attachment rehabilitation assessment
A pubic symptom is present, but the recorded resisted activity is completed. It does not reproduce the deep ache stopping the limiting work task.

before: **KEY:** Continue observation while advancing rehabilitation
Function improves without changing the hernia finding. The interval response supports the current conservative approach rather than using persistent imaging alone as an indication to alter the plan.
Start repair planning while advancing rehabilitation
A persistent protrusion can attract repair planning, but the actual functional trajectory does not establish a new hernia-related limitation that explains a need to change this initial plan.
Start repair planning before advancing rehabilitation
This gives an unchanged imaging finding priority over the improving function and pauses a program that is helping. It assumes the hernia must be corrected before activity can progress.
after: **KEY:** Hernia assessment with continued graded activity

Completed shifts on modified duties do not demonstrate recovery of the avoided lifting task. The current pressure/contour event supplies a hernia-related functional concern despite improved running and a coexisting attachment symptom.
Hernia observation with continued graded activity
This mistakes attendance on modified duties and longer jogging for unrestricted work function. It overlooks the task that remains unperformed and the observed groin event on attempting it.
Attachment reassessment with continued graded activity
The persistent adduction symptom is a credible reason for musculoskeletal review, but the actual remaining crate-handling interruption occurs with the separate groin pressure/contour event.

contextRevisions.comparisonBasis: Before is the exact draft assessed in independent review six. The v10 after is projected from current assembled source.

before: **KEY:** Refer during ongoing rehabilitation
The remaining functional interruption tracks the reducible protrusion despite improvement in the coexisting attachment/joint symptoms. Elective assessment need not await completion of that treatment.
Refer after rehabilitation is completed
Residual musculoskeletal symptoms can coexist with a hernia that already limits function. Treating them first as an absolute referral prerequisite delays the separately supported hernia assessment.
Refer after repeat imaging documents progression
Anatomical enlargement is not required before discussing an already demonstrated activity-limiting inguinal hernia. This mistakes imaging change for the relevant functional criterion.
after: **KEY:** Attachment assessment alongside the current exercise program

The limiting transfer pain is reproduced by adduction and occurs without the contour; a transfer can be completed with the contour present. These observations favor reviewing the attachment-related limitation rather than assigning all burden to the hernia.
Inguinal-hernia assessment alongside the current exercise program
The earlier hernia-associated episodes make this credible, but the later task-specific dissociation weakens attribution of the current transfer difficulty to the protrusion.
Hip-joint assessment alongside the current exercise program
A separate deep ache exists, but it is not the pain reproduced in the low-chair transfers. Selecting it confuses a positive examination finding with the currently limiting symptom.

contextRevisions.inference: Distinguish the later transfer limitation from the earlier reduction-responsive episodes using tasks performed with and without the visible contour. Then Compare the reproduced medial pain with the separate hip ache to choose the lead care target.
contextRevisions.focus: Hernia and musculoskeletal clinicians must confirm the proposed care priority and competing plans. These are selected next assessments, not compulsory operations, promises of pain relief or rules prohibiting elective consultation. No size, duration, imaging-growth or rehabilitation-completion threshold is used.
contextRevisions.whatChanged: Clarify initial supervised versus maintenance care and use later crossed task/contour observations to select among three active care targets. Earlier hernia-associated symptoms no longer automatically assign the current limitation.

contextRevisions.comparisonBasis: Before is the exact draft assessed in independent review six. The v10 after is projected from current assembled source.

before: **KEY:** Refer during ongoing rehabilitation
The remaining functional interruption tracks the reducible protrusion despite improvement in the coexisting attachment/joint symptoms. Elective assessment need not await completion of that treatment.
Refer after rehabilitation is completed
Residual musculoskeletal symptoms can coexist with a hernia that already limits function. Treating them first as an absolute referral prerequisite delays the separately supported hernia assessment.
Refer after repeat imaging documents progression
Anatomical enlargement is not required before discussing an already demonstrated activity-limiting inguinal hernia. This mistakes imaging change for the relevant functional criterion.
after: **KEY:** Prioritize hernia assessment while continuing rehabilitation

The earlier painless protrusion is not proof that all later episodes are incidental. A different, now limiting groin symptom tracks the protrusion after the original flexion-provoked complaint improves.
Prioritize attachment reassessment while continuing rehabilitation
This carries forward the earlier MRI-associated pain assignment despite resolution of its reproduced functional problem and a different current site/provocation.
Prioritize hip-joint assessment while continuing rehabilitation
A hip-related ache remains, but the patient and observed task distinguish it from the superficial symptom stopping work.

before: **KEY:** Sampled edge explained; assess residual-lesion architecture

This extends a benign fragment to the changing unrepresented center and limits assessment to tissue that does not contain that center.

after: **KEY:** Correlate the submitted site with the procedure photograph

Deeper levels can answer a question about tissue in the block, but they cannot establish that it came from the changing center when the location records disagree.
Reassess the existing fragment with additional immunostains
Ancillary stains can contribute to classification, but they do not settle which clinical sector was represented. The benign fragment need not be erroneous to leave the changing focus unexplained.

before: **KEY:** Sampled sector in situ; residual-lesion invasion unassessed
The report establishes epidermis-confined melanoma in the sampled sector. Its mapping does not establish that the separate raised residual focus is also epidermis confined.
Sampled sector in situ; residual-lesion invasion excluded
This correctly identifies the submitted compartment but extends it to a different unrepresented part of the lesion.
Sampled sector invasive; residual-lesion invasion unassessed
The remaining focus is unassessed, but dermis being present in the specimen is not itself evidence that melanoma invaded it.
Sampled sector invasive; residual-lesion invasion excluded
This confuses represented dermis with invaded dermis and simultaneously makes an unsupported clearance claim for the residual component.
after: **KEY:** Excisional biopsy of the complete lesion

The sampled sector is epidermis confined, but its report does not establish the invasive status of the raised residual component. Complete diagnostic removal is feasible and can supply the architecture and maximum invasion information needed before selecting treatment extent.
Wide local excision for melanoma in situ

This converts a valid local epidermal diagnosis into a whole-lesion treatment classification before the raised residual focus is represented. A therapeutic plan based on that extension may use the wrong disease extent.
Full-thickness incisional biopsy of the raised focus

Targeting the raised component is a credible way to seek invasion information, but it again samples part of a lesion whose complete diagnostic removal is feasible, leaving whole-lesion architecture and maximum depth less fully represented.

contextRevisions.comparisonBasis: Before is the exact draft assessed in independent review six. The v10 after is projected from current assembled source.

before: **KEY:** Retain at least 0.6 mm; await the final maximum depth
The measured invasive component is valid as a lower bound because tumor reaches the cut base. The unsampled continuation can increase the maximum; it cannot erase the measured extent.
Retain at most 0.6 mm; await the final maximum depth
This reverses the bound. Tumor at the cut base can continue deeper, so the observed depth cannot be used as an upper limit.
Retain exactly 0.6 mm; use it as the maximum depth
The number is a distance to a tumor-positive cut surface, not necessarily the deepest tumor in the lesion. Using it as a complete maximum can understate the lesion.
Retain no measured depth; await the final maximum depth
The incomplete base prevents an exact whole-lesion maximum, but it does not invalidate the already measured invasive extent. Blanket uncertainty loses a valid lower bound.
after: **KEY:** At least 1.8 mm; nodal-staging discussion supported

The greatest demonstrated invasive extent is not erased by a later shallower transected fragment. Even though the whole-lesion maximum is not final, the established depth is already in the range supporting a sentinel-node discussion in this clinically node-negative setting.
At least 0.6 mm; nodal-staging discussion supported
The general discussion direction does not repair the depth record: this drops the greater demonstrated invasive extent simply because another specimen was later or transected.
At least 1.8 mm; nodal-staging discussion deferred
This preserves the demonstrated extent but treats uncertainty about a possibly greater maximum as a reason to ignore a discussion boundary already crossed by known evidence.
At least 0.6 mm; nodal-staging discussion deferred
This both replaces the greater demonstrated extent with a later smaller value and uses incomplete maximum-depth assessment to defer an already supported discussion.

contextRevisions.comparisonBasis: Before is the exact draft assessed in independent review six. The v10 after is projected from current assembled source.

before: **KEY:** Region R through the anterior corridor
This region shows a contrast-related signal increase and can be approached through the involved muscle, integrating viability with a tract that avoids a separate unaffected compartment.
Region P through the anterior corridor

The corridor stays in the involved compartment, but pre-existing T1 brightness without a contrast-related increase is not the supplied evidence of a viable target. Brightness alone is not enhancement.
Region Q through the medial corridor
This region enhances, but its proposed route crosses a separate adductor compartment. Target enhancement does not remove the tract-planning consequence.
after: **KEY:** Axial T1 before and after contrast, both with fat suppression

A comparison with consistent sequence settings can distinguish intrinsic precontrast brightness from contrast-related change. The outside pair changes both contrast status and suppression, so brightness differences cannot simply be assigned to enhancement.
Axial and coronal T1 after contrast, both with fat suppression
Orthogonal anatomy is useful, but two postcontrast views do not supply a comparable precontrast baseline for the intrinsically bright area.
Axial T1 without fat suppression and fluid-sensitive images before contrast

These contribute tissue characterization but retain an unsuppressed T1 baseline. Different sequence weighting does not supply the comparable pre/postcontrast information needed for this targeting question.

comparisonBasis: Before is the exact draft assessed in independent review six. The v10 after is projected from current assembled source.

before: **KEY:** Current-list manual entry versus current-list prefill

The pilot separates a record-source agreement problem from an entry-time opportunity. Testing prefill from the current reconciled source evaluates whether the faster method can retain the agreement of that source.
Prior-list manual entry versus prior-list prefill
This repeats the observed time reduction while keeping the source associated with poorer agreement. It does not test whether the speed gain can coexist with the current source's agreement.
Prior-list manual entry versus current-list manual entry
This repeats the observed source contrast without evaluating the faster entry method using the current source. It leaves the practical adaptation question unanswered.
after: **KEY:** Source L manual entry versus source L prefill

This retains an input with the better agreement record and tests the demonstrated entry-time opportunity where the recorded burden remains greater. It directly evaluates a method change within that workflow without assuming success.
Source N manual entry versus source N prefill

This is an equally new controlled method comparison using another high-agreement source. It is a credible later test, but its manual entry already has the lower observed burden, making it a weaker first target for the stated improvement aim.
Source N manual entry versus source L prefill

This is also a new comparison and could benchmark complete workflows. It changes source and entry method together, rather than establish the effect of adapting the higher-burden manual workflow against its own baseline.

inference: Separate the observed source-agreement pattern from the entry-method time pattern, then identify which high-agreement manual workflow still carries the greater burden. Then Choose the new comparison that tests adapting that workflow against its own baseline rather than prioritize an already lower-burden workflow or change source and method together.
focus: QI/owner review must confirm the prioritization under the stated reduce-work/retain-agreement aim. whatChanged: Add an efficient high-agreement manual workflow and compare three genuinely new tests. Two controlled method tests now compete, requiring both agreement and burden data before prioritizing the first adaptation.

cues: cues 1: Every comparison now introduces an untested prefill workflow. Two are within-source controlled method comparisons; neither novelty nor a generic keep-one-factor rule selects L over N without outcomes.
